title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook — Process, Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, Game Days, Status Page & Customer Comms
author: Aisha Kumar
content:
Summary
-------
This Playbook documents Redwood Inference's standard on-call and incident response process, runbook templates, postmortem expectations, rotation rules, game-day plans, and canonical status-page / customer communication templates. It is intended for on-call engineers, SREs, product owners, support, and customer success staff who participate in detection, response, escalation and customer communications for operational incidents.

Goals
- Restore service quickly and safely while minimizing customer impact.
- Preserve post-incident learning via consistent postmortems and remediation.
- Ensure predictable escalation and communication for internal and external stakeholders.
- Regularly validate procedures through game days and runbook exercises.

Scope
This document covers: incident severity definitions, alert routing and ownership, runbook structure and examples, on-call rotation policy, escalation matrix, postmortem template and timeline, game-day guidelines, and status page / customer comms templates. For security incidents, follow the Security incident response policy in security-and-compliance/incident-response-security.

1) Incident severity and SLO mapping
----------------------------------
Severity definitions (use for prioritization and SLA targets):
- SEV1 (Critical): Service is down or core inference path is unavailable for >1% of customers or significant data-loss risk.
  - Target: page immediately. Acknowledge <= 15 minutes, restore or mitigation plan within 60 minutes.
- SEV2 (Major): Major degradation (latency >3x median, 50% error-rate on a critical path) affecting many customers or large feature regressions.
  - Target: acknowledge <= 30 minutes, mitigation plan within 4 hours.
- SEV3 (Minor): Functional degradation affecting small subset of customers or non-core features.
  - Target: acknowledge <= 4 hours, fix in next sprint or scheduled maintenance window.
- SEV4 (Informational): Observability alerts, warnings, or request-for-info that do not affect customers.
  - Target: handle during business hours.

SLO references (examples): availability 99.9% for production inference endpoints, median p95 latency < 200 ms for text-generation on dedicated tier. When an incident threatens SLO attainment for a customer group, escalate to SEV1/SEV2 depending on impact.

2) Roles and responsibilities
-----------------------------
- First Responder (On-call Engineer): Primary responsibility for triage, runbook execution, and initial mitigation.
- Secondary (Escalation): Senior engineer or SRE who supports complex mitigation or fails over systems.
- Incident Commander (IC): Coordinates the incident (can be first responder initially for brief incidents). Owns communication cadence, ensures postmortem.
- Subject Matter Experts (SMEs): Model-serving, GPU-fleet, infra, networking, or database owners as required.
- Customer Success (CS) / Support: Prepares customer-facing comms, coordinates priority customer outreach.
- Eng Manager / Product Manager: Decision authority for rollbacks, mitigation prioritization, and business communications.

3) Alert routing and on-call paging
-----------------------------------
Alerting rules must map to severity. Typical routing:
- SEV1 -> pager to SRE rotation + 2x primary service on-call (phone/Slack + SMS).
- SEV2 -> pager to primary on-call (Slack + email) and notify SRE.
- SEV3/4 -> ticket creation (Jira), notify appropriate Slack channel.

Escalation timeline (default):
1. Page primary on-call. If no acknowledgement in 15 minutes (SEV1) escalate to secondary.
2. If still unresolved after 1 hour (SEV1) IC engages Eng Manager and Customer Success.
3. For SEV2, escalation after 30–60 minutes per impact.

Contact architecture: maintain an oncall roster in the shared calendar and PagerDuty. The on-call owner must keep the roster up-to-date and publish expected time off >= 7 days before coverage gaps.

4) Runbook template and canonical checks
----------------------------------------
Every service must have a runbook with the following flat structure (single-file README or confluence page):
- title (short)
- service owner(s)
- contact (on-call rotation identifier)
- severity triage checklist
- quick health checks (API endpoints, key metrics)
- immediate mitigation steps (ordered)
- diagnostics commands and snippets
- rollback and failover steps
- post-incident evidence collection (logs, traces, alerts)
- postmortem link placeholder

Example runbook excerpt (production inference service):
- Quick health checks:
  - curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health | less
  - grafana: Cluster -> inference-pool -> error-rate p95
  - kubectl get pods -n inference -l app=inference --field-selector=status.phase!=Running

- Immediate mitigation (ordered):
  1. Validate alert: check Prometheus / Grafana dashboards for error spikes, backend GPU node failures, and autoscaler logs.
  2. If GPU node OOM or kernel panic: isolate node (set cordon), fail traffic off node (kubectl drain) and increase capacity via dedicated autoscaler (if reserved).
     - kubectl cordon <node>
     - kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
  3. If model inference containers are crashing repeatedly, restart deployment: kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-service -n inference
  4. If latency spike due to batching misconfiguration, adjust runtime batching parameters via the runtime control plane: curl -X POST https://runtime-control/api/v1/config -d '{"batch_ms":40}'
  5. As a short-term mitigation, switch routing policy to a lower-cost/compatible model variant: set-routing-policy --service inference --variant small --reason "Incident mitigation"

Diagnostic commands (examples):
- logs: kubectl logs -n inference deployment/inference-service --since=10m | tail -n 200
- pods: kubectl describe pod <pod> -n inference
- metrics: curl -sS "http://prometheus/api/v1/query?query=rate(http_requests_total[5m])" | jq .
- tracing: open Jaeger -> trace ID search for recent 5xxs

5) Escalation matrix (example)
----------------------------
- Level 1: Primary on-call (service owner) — 15 min ack (SEV1)
- Level 2: SRE lead / Secondary on-call — 30 min escalation
- Level 3: Eng Manager / Tech Lead (decision for rollback) — 1 hour
- Level 4: VP Eng + Customer Success Director — major outage / exec comms

6) Communication cadence and templates
-------------------------------------
Internal comms (Slack channel #incidents):
- Initial alert: one-line summary (SEV, impacted services, initial ETA if known). Example:
  [SEV1] inference-api: 50% 5xx (region us-east-1). Primary on-call: @alice. IC: @aisha.
- 15-min update: action taken and next step.
- Hourly until mitigation "in progress" or "service degraded" changes to resolved.
- Postmortem posted when investigation is complete.

Status page / Customer-facing templates (public status page + email):
- Public status (short):
  Title: Partial outage — inference API (us-east-1)
  Summary: We are investigating increased error rates affecting text-generation for customers in US-East. Impact: reduced throughput and elevated 5xx rates for some requests.
  Next update: in 30 minutes.
  Mitigation: traffic has been re-routed to a fallback pool and we are actively rolling a fix.
  Update template: [Time UTC] Update: mitigation in place; remaining errors are limited to 5% of requests; working on full recovery.
  Resolved template: [Time UTC] Resolved: The issue has been resolved; services are returning to normal metrics. We are following up with a post-incident report.

- Email / Customer success template (for affected customers):
  Subject: Incident update — Redwood Inference (inference API)
  Body: Hello <Customer Name>,

  We are currently investigating an issue impacting inference API requests in us-east-1. You may see increased errors or latency. Our engineering team has rerouted traffic and applied mitigations; we will send an update in 30 minutes. If you have urgent needs, reply to this message or contact your CSM.

  Thank you for your patience,
  Redwood Inference Operations

7) Postmortem expectations and template
-------------------------------------
A postmortem is required for any SEV1/SEV2 incident or any incident that meets the "customer-impact" threshold. Postmortem must be published within 7 business days and include mitigation, timeline, root cause, contributing factors, and action items with owners and due dates.

Postmortem template (flat fields for easy ingestion):
- Title
- Incident ID
- Severity
- Start time / End time (UTC)
- Impacted services and customer scope
- Summary (brief)
- Timeline of events (minute resolution)
- Root cause (analysis)
- Corrective actions (short-term mitigations and long-term fixes)
- Action items (owner, action, due date)
- Detection and monitoring gaps
- Lessons learned

8) Evidence collection checklist
-------------------------------
During and immediately after an incident collect and attach:
- Prometheus/Grafana dashboards and time-range snapshots
- Logs (kubectl logs / logstore exports) for implicated services (archive last 24 hours)
- Traces (Jaeger) and representative trace IDs
- PagerDuty timeline and Slack transcripts (export)
- Any config changes, rollouts, or infra events with timestamps

9) On-call rotations and rules
-----------------------------
- Rotation cadence: 1-week rotations for primary on-call engineers; 2-week rotations for SRE escalation.
- Handover: on-call engineers must perform a documented handover in Slack and update duty calendar at start/end of shift. Handover notes should include ongoing incidents, maintenance windows, and any temporary mitigations.
- Time-off policy: coordinate with backups at least 7 days in advance. For planned longer absences (>2 weeks), arrange for a designated replacement and notify the on-call roster owner.
- Swap policy: engineers may swap shifts via the on-call scheduling tool; the person who accepts the swap becomes the responsibility owner.

10) Game days and runbook drills
-------------------------------
Purpose: Validate runbooks, detection fidelity, rotation readiness, and cross-team coordination.
Game day cadence and checklist:
- Quarterly game day executed by SRE with 2–3 simulated incidents (production-like but isolated).
- Pre-game checklist: scope, safety net (rate limits, circuit breakers), observation-only mode, and customer communication freeze if needed.
- Runbook validation: each runbook sprint exercises one scenario end-to-end.
- Success metrics: mean time to acknowledge, mean time to mitigation, correctness of actions, quality of comms.
- After action: publish game-day report and update runbooks within 7 days for observed gaps.

11) Templates: Incident internal Slack posts, public status updates, and customer emails
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Internal alert (Slack) example:
[SEV1] inference-api (us-east-1) — 2026-03-04T14:03Z
Impact: 60% 5xx on /v1/generate, elevated latency.
Primary on-call: @aisha (paged). IC: @aisha. Secondary: @devon.
Initial actions: investigating GPU node failures; cordoned node(s) and drained; autoscaler increased by +3 nodes.
Next update: in 15 minutes.

Public status page (plain text example):
Title: Partial outage — Inference API (us-east-1)
Status: Degraded Performance
Started: 2026-03-04T14:00Z
Update 1 (14:15Z): We have identified elevated 5xx responses and have re-routed traffic to fallback pools. Mitigation in progress; next update at 14:45Z.
Resolved (15:12Z): We mitigated the issue and metrics returned to normal. Root cause: autoscaler regression causing slow pod start times. Full postmortem forthcoming.

Customer email (short):
Subject: Incident resolved — inference API (us-east-1)
Hi <Customer>,
We resolved the incident impacting inference API in us-east-1. Systems are operating normally; we are preparing a postmortem and will share findings and mitigations. Apologies for the impact.
Best,
Redwood Operations

12) Runbook and postmortem ownership SLAs
-----------------------------------------
- Runbook creation: new service must provide a minimum runbook before going to prod; owner must be listed in the service README.
- Runbook review: annual review required by service owner; reviewers include SRE and at least one other team.
- Postmortem publication: SEV1/2 within 7 business days; SEV3 optionally summarized during sprint retro.

13) Metrics and reporting
-------------------------
Track incident metrics on the SRE dashboard:
- MTTA (mean time to acknowledge) by severity
- MTTM (mean time to mitigation) by severity
- MTTR (mean time to resolve)
- Number of repeated incidents tied to the same root cause

14) Related pages and references
--------------------------------
- infra-standards: Terraform and network change rollback playbook
- eng-sre/SLO-and-error-budgets: SLO policy and error budget enforcement
- security-and-compliance/incident-response-security: security incident process

Appendix A: Quick checklist for first responder (one-page)
---------------------------------------------------------
1) Acknowledge alert and post status to #incidents.
2) Identify scope: run quick health checks and confirm severity.
3) Apply short-term mitigation from runbook.
4) If mitigation not successful in 15 minutes (SEV1), escalate to secondary.
5) Preserve logs/traces and collect evidence.
6) Notify IC and Customer Success if customers affected.
7) After resolution, create incident ticket and link to postmortem.

----------------------------------------------
